claims.text: Boride-based components are used in an uncoated condition in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
Applying a thin, uniform Al2O3 coating by chemical vapor deposition will improve the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components relative to uncoated components.
Chemical vapor deposition can form a controlled-thickness Al2O3 coating on a boride-based component.
The deposited Al2O3 coating will create a stable, continuous interface on the boride substrate.
The continuous Al2O3 interface will act as a physical barrier between molten aluminum and the boride substrate.
The Al2O3 coating will reduce direct chemical interaction between molten aluminum and the boride material.
The Al2O3 coating will reduce wetting of the boride material by molten aluminum.
The Al2O3 barrier will limit aluminum infiltration into the boride substrate.
The Al2O3 barrier will limit reaction between molten aluminum and the underlying boride.
Limiting wetting, infiltration, and interfacial reaction will inhibit molten-aluminum corrosion.
Coated samples will exhibit lower mass loss or reduced corrosion penetration depth than uncoated samples under identical exposure conditions.
The corrosion-resistance improvement will persist only while the Al2O3 coating remains intact and stable under the operating temperature and chemical exposure.
